newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FAXON BREAKS VICTORY DROUGHT IN NEW ORLEANS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FAXON BREAKS VICTORY DROUGHT IN NEW ORLEANS.

text.p: Brad Faxon won his first PGA Tour event in almost five years Sunday, taking the $1.5 million Freeport-McDermott Classic by three strokes over Sweden's Jesper Parnevik and Bill Glasson.
Faxon shot a final-round 69 to finish at 16-under-par 272, a 72-hole scoring record at English Turn G.C. by two strokes.
"It's about time, let me tell you. This is great. I've finished second an awful lot and had a lot of chances.

"It gets to a point where it really starts to bug you," said Faxon, who had finished second five times since his last victory and last year set the record for most money earned in a single season without a victory.
Parnevik's 66 on Sunday gave him his third runner-up finish of the year and sixth top five, pushing him into third place on the money list with $833,798.
Glasson is playing the tour on a medical exemption following elbow surgery last May, the 11th operation of his career.

Faxon's only bogey of the day, which included 28 holes of golf because of rain on Saturday, came on the 72nd hole, cutting his winning margin from four strokes to three. Long considered one of the tour's best putters, Faxon needed just 101 putts this week.
Faxon was already exempt for next week's Masters, and goes to Augusta with more confidence than he has ever had. His best finish there was a tie for ninth in 1993.
"I like my chances a lot this year. It's a golf course I really enjoy. I like putting those greens, and the course suits the shape of my shots," said Faxon.
Of the two runners-up, only Parnevik had an invitation to the Masters.

"After I three-putted the 14th hole Brad just had too big a lead and I was just playing for a good finish. It's a good feeling going into the Masters, but I don't know what to expect since I've never been there before," said Parnevik.

Had Glasson won he would have earned the last exemption into the Masters, but probably would not have been able to play. "I can't play two weeks in a row yet. I'm hoping to be able to do that by May," said Glasson.

Finishing in a tie for seventh at 10 under par was Spain's Jose Maria Olazabal, who has now played 16 rounds since returning from an 18-month absence from golf, and has a collective score of 51 under par for his four tournaments.

When Olazabal's feet hurt so much he could hardly walk, he was initially mis-diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis, and thought he would never play golf again. His feet actually hurt because of a hernia in his back, it was later determined.

Olazabal, the 1994 Masters winner, said on Sunday as he headed out for Augusta National, "The feet are not the problem, it is the game that is maybe not ready. I'm just looking forward to having a good time and enjoying the week."
